title: Solstice Health - Procurement: MSA/DPA, SLAs, Pricing & Onboarding
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA and proposed DPA by 2027-10-04
SE to share SOC2 + penetration test report links
Schedule technical pilot kickoff (2-week) week of 2027-10-11
Pricing approval doc to be submitted to Solstice finance by 2027-10-06
action_items: Maya Chen: Send redline MSA & DPA, include SLA addendum - due 2027-10-04
Liam Patel: Share benchmark spreadsheet and recommended instance sizing for pilot - due 2027-10-03
Sofia Reyes: Provide any additional security questions list / scope for pen test - due 2027-10-05
Evan Mills: Review DPA redline and flag any legal concerns - due 2027-10-08
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-09-30
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Karen Ortiz (Solstice Procurement), Dr. Anil Rao (CTO), Evan Mills (Legal), Sofia Reyes (Security)
summary: Procurement call to finalize MSA/DPA redlines, confirm SLA requirements for a pilot, and outline pricing approval and onboarding steps. Customer requested SOC2 evidence, KMS details, and an SLA addendum with latency targets. Redwood to send redlines and security docs; schedule 2-week pilot. Key blockers: legal redlines on data residency and indemnity, internal pricing signoff timeline.
topics: Pricing approval and internal procurement timeline
Security evidence (SOC2, PEN test, KMS integration)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll give it a quick intro - I'm Maya, AE on this account, with Liam our solutions engineer and Jordan on customer success.
[00:10] Karen (Solstice - Procurement): Hi all, thanks. We have about an hour - we've got a couple of objectives: legal redlines on the MSA/DPA, confirm SLA, and understand the onboarding/pilot timeline.
[00:20] Liam (Redwood SE): Great, we'll cover technical implications of the DPA items too, like KMS and private VPC.
[00:35] Evan (Legal): Quick note - we'll be focusing on data residency and indemnity.
[01:00] Maya: Perfect. I'll start with the MSA status - Redwood sent the standard MSA last week, you sent back a redline with three major asks: tighter data residency, expanded indemnity, and a shorter termination notice. We can walk through each.
[02:05] Karen: Right. Data residency is the biggest for us - PHI flows into some of our analytics pipelines and our compliance team requires EU/US regional residency, and also an audit trail.
[02:35] Liam: For residency we support region pinning on Redwood Dedicated and Private; for hosted we have geo-routing but not strict contractual residency unless you choose Dedicated or Private deployment. There was a note in the redline asking for contractual guarantees - that's doable on Dedicated or Private, yes.
[03:02] Dr. Anil Rao (CTO): If we do Dedicated, what's the expected lead time and cost delta?
[03:18] Maya: Dedicated typically has a lead time depending on capacity - for a pilot we often do a short-term reserved pool or we can run a small pilot on hosted with strict routing and then move to Dedicated for production. Cost delta is in the quote - roughly 30-50% uplift vs hosted depending on commit.
[03:45] Evan: On indemnity, your standard MSA limits liability and we asked for increased carveouts around data breaches.
[03:58] Maya: We can review specific language - we usually have a cap tied to subscription fees, but for enterprise deals we can negotiate specific carveouts. I'll flag that for legal to propose alternate wording.
[04:20] Karen: Great. On DPA, Sofia's team has a list of required subprocessors and wants confirmation your KMS supports customer-managed keys.
[04:35] Sofia (Security): We need to see KMS integration details. Does Redwood support BYOK across Dedicated and Private?
[04:45] Liam: Short answer: yes for Private; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) depending on deployment. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can discuss Bring-Your-Own-Key on certain enterprise tiers.
[05:10] Sofia: Can we get penetration test results and SOC2 report?
[05:18] Jordan (CSM): We'll share links - SOC2 type II and the latest pen test summary. I'll include the signed attestation and a redacted report link.
[05:30] Maya: I'll drop those into the repo after the call (link in notes).
[06:00] Evan: SLA - we requested 99.9% uptime and latency targets for p95 generation under the SLA, plus credits.
[06:12] Liam: Our standard SLA is 99.5% for hosted with options to move to 99.9% in Dedicated with higher commit. Latency SLOs are usually expressed as targets per route and workload; we can add explicit p95 tokens latency targets into an SLA addendum. Credits are standard - sliding scale based on downtime.
[06:45] Dr. Rao: We need p95 under 200ms for short text generation for our UI - is that realistic?
[07:00] Liam: For small payloads, with Dedicated and appropriate instance sizing, p95 under 200ms is achievable. We'll need to run a benchmark with your payloads. I'll include recommended instance types and batching config.
[07:25] Karen: Timeline: procurement needs pricing approval by 2027-10-06 to make the quarterly budget.
[07:34] Maya: Understood - we'll prioritize the pricing paperwork.
[07:50] Karen: On onboarding, we propose a 2-week pilot with a limited dataset and production-like traffic to validate latency and costs.
[08:02] Liam: Sounds good. For pilot scope, here's what we suggest - two routes: one for short UI prompts and one for longer clinical summarization. We'll provide a checklist for test data, expected volumes, and KV caching suggestions.
[08:30] Dr. Rao: For the summarization route, cost per token will be sensitive. We need visibility into worst-case token usage.
[08:45] Maya: We'll share an estimated cost model and a spreadsheet with cost per 1k tokens per model variant plus expected compute.
[09:10] Evan: Legal again - we need the DPA to explicitly list subprocessors and also the timeline for notification if you change subprocessors.
[09:20] Liam: The DPA template includes subprocessors as a schedule; we can add a 30-day notification clause before onboarding a new subprocessor.
[09:35] Evan: Good. Also retention: can we set a maximum retention window for request logs?
[09:44] Maya: Yes, retention windows are configurable; for enterprise we can set contractually agreed windows and provide deletion attestations.
[10:00] Karen: On exportability - our internal auditors want a data export procedure in case of termination.
[10:10] Jordan: We provide tooling and documented export processes; we'll include a runbook and sample export link.
[10:25] Sofia: A question on encryption in transit - do you support mutual TLS for private deployments?
[10:32] Liam: Yes, mutual TLS is supported in Private and Dedicated with custom certs. For hosted, we use TLS 1.2/1.3 with client certs available on some tiers.
[11:00] Maya: Let me jump in with the commercial ask - Karen, you mentioned you need pricing approval by 10/06. We'll prepare a formal pricing sheet and an SOW for the pilot and push the MSA redline concurrently.
[11:18] Karen: Will you be able to include an SLA addendum in the MSA redline package?
[11:25] Maya: Yes, we'll include an SLA addendum - Liam will propose the exact p95 latency numbers for the pilot routes.
[11:40] Evan: On indemnity and breach notifications: we need 72 hours notification for incidents affecting PHI.
[11:50] Maya: Noted - I'll take that back to legal but we typically do 72 hours or sooner for incidents; we'll surface that in the redline.
[12:10] Dr. Rao: A practical question - if we start on hosted strictly for pilot, will we have any data commingling concerns?
[12:22] Liam: Hosted is multi-tenant but data isolation is logical. For pilot we can enable strong encryption and strict access controls; for production with residency requirements, we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[12:45] Karen: Procurement needs an approved vendor packet - can you share your insurance certificates and SOC2 attestation?
[12:55] Jordan: Absolutely, I'll attach insurance cert, SOC2 link, pen test summary, and the security questionnaire answers.
[13:10] Maya: We'll also include product security bullet points and KMS architecture diagram.
[13:30] Karen: About pricing - can you give us list pricing and an example committed annual spend that gets us to the 99.9% SLA?
[13:40] Maya: Yes, I'll put together two pricing tiers: a self-serve hosted tier for pilot, and a committed Dedicated tier with pricing for 99.9% SLA - the latter will include commit discounts and a path to burst capacity.
[14:05] Evan: Legal will review the DPA redline and likely propose edits to subprocessors and liability sections. Expect back in a week.
[14:15] Maya: That's fine. We'll aim to have Redwood's redline out in 3 business days.
[14:35] Liam: Technical aside - for the latency numbers we discussed, I want to run your example prompts and we should test both quantized variants and FP16 models; quantization can reduce cost but may affect quality on clinical text.
[15:00] Dr. Rao: Understood, we'll include a set of representative prompts in the pilot data.
[15:22] Karen: On procurement approvals, I need a short vendor one-pager we can attach to the approval packet summarizing security, SLA, and costs.
[15:33] Maya: We'll prepare a concise one-pager and a short vendor summary doc for procurement.
[15:45] Sofia: One more security ask - can Redwood support an on-prem connector for clients who want to keep raw data on their network?
[15:55] Liam: We have an on-prem Private deployment option that can run inside customer network; connector architecture varies, we'll share a reference architecture doc.
[16:10] Evan: About insurance - do you have cyber liability limits and what are they?
[16:18] Jordan: Current limit is $10M cyber liability, will attach cert.
[16:25] Karen: Great. If we get the redline and the SOC2 by 10/04, our legal and procurement teams can push pricing approval by 10/06 - that's the ask.
[16:37] Maya: We'll prioritize that.
[16:50] Liam: For the pilot SOW, suggested milestones: week 0 setup and onboarding, week 1 ramp and test, week 2 performance validation and handoff.
[17:05] Dr. Rao: And acceptance criteria?
[17:10] Liam: Acceptance based on achieving p95 target for route A and cost within agreed threshold for route B, plus successful integration with your KMS for key handling if applicable.
[17:28] Karen: Any blockers on Redwood side for the 10/06 timeline?
[17:34] Maya: None from commercial; legal will need a couple days but we'll aim to get everything to you by 10/04.
[17:50] Evan: We'll review and send back DPA redline by 10/08 at the latest.
[18:02] Maya: Ok. I'll summarize actions in the meeting notes.
[18:15] [Brief silence / paper rustle]
[20:00] Liam: A quick note on metrics - during the pilot we'll surface token breakdowns, cost per call, and KV cache hit rates so you can see unit economics.
[20:18] Dr. Rao: Good - that level of telemetry is important for our platform team.
[21:00] Karen: Who is the single point of contact for onboarding?
[21:08] Jordan: I'll be your CSM, so Jordan will drive onboarding and coordinate SE time.
[21:20] Jordan: I'll set up a Confluence space and share links.
[22:10] Maya: Next, procurement wants a list of signing authorities and contract flow - I'll include a simple contract flow diagram.
[22:30] Karen: Perfect.
[23:10] Evan: For the SLA credits, we ask that they are cash or creditable amounts; avoid service credits that can't be used for the initial year.
[23:22] Maya: We'll note that preference. Enterprise deals often allow negotiation there.
[24:00] Sofia: A question on logs access - can your security team provide read-only log access for our auditors?
[24:10] Liam: We can provide log export and aggregated telemetry; for direct read access we'll need to surface a secure method - often log exports to your logging system is the cleanest path.
[24:35] Karen: Ok. Any other questions from the Solstice side?
[24:40] Dr. Rao: One more - can we do an internal procurement review meeting with Redwood legal next week?
[24:50] Evan: Yes, let's tentatively schedule for 2027-10-05.
[25:00] Maya: I'll coordinate availability and include a proposed agenda: redline review, SLA addendum, pilot SOW.
[25:20] Karen: On pricing, will there be a minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[25:28] Maya: Dedicated typically comes with a monthly commit based on GPU hours; for pilot we can do a short term commit or burst capacity. The pricing sheet will clarify.
[26:00] Liam: Technically, if you want guaranteed p95 200ms, we'll size appropriately and factor in batch sizes. For the UI route batching should be minimal to preserve latency.
[26:20] Dr. Rao: Makes sense.
[26:50] Jordan: I'll attach the security docs in the follow up: SOC2 link, pen test summary, insurance cert, and the vendor one-pager.
[27:05] Karen: Awesome.
[27:30] Maya: Final commercial note - any procurement constraints on payment terms? Net30 is standard, any need for Net60?
[27:40] Karen: Procurement prefers Net60 for new vendors, but we can expedite to Net30 for pilots if needed.
[28:00] Maya: Good to know - we'll flag billing options in the pricing sheet.
[29:10] Evan: We'll send legal redline by 10/08 and confirm internal signoffs.
[29:20] Maya: Thanks. I'll send Redwood's redline by 10/04.
[29:35] Karen: Can you also include a summary of support SLAs (response times) for SE/CS and escalation paths?
[29:45] Jordan: Yes, standard support tiers: business hours vs 24/7 for enterprise, with P1 response times in the addendum - I'll include the escalation matrix.
[30:10] Liam: I'll add recommended monitoring hooks and tracing integrations for your dev team.
[30:30] Dr. Rao: We'll want to instrument end-to-end traces for latency attribution.
[30:40] Liam: We'll share sample tracing hooks.
[31:05] Karen: Anything else from Redwood?
[31:10] Maya: No, we covered the big items. We'll follow up with all docs.
[31:25] Karen: Thanks everyone.
[31:35] [Crosstalk / wrap up]
[32:00] Maya: Quick recap of next steps: Maya to send MSA/DPA redline and SLA addendum by 10/04; Liam to share benchmark spreadsheet and instance sizing by 10/03; Jordan to attach SOC2/pen test/insurance; Solstice legal to return redlines by 10/08; schedule legal touchpoint on 10/05.
[32:30] Karen: That timelines works.
[33:00] Maya: We'll also send the vendor one-pager for procurement.
[33:10] Dr. Rao: Looking forward to the pilot.
[33:20] Evan: Thanks all.
[33:30] Jordan: I'll send meeting notes and the doc pack after the call.
[34:00] [Meeting ends - informal goodbyes]

Notes / Links referenced in call:
- SOC2 report (link): https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-2027

- Draft MSA/DPA (shared in-email)

End of transcript.
